body:
`docker-image-build-dev.yml` triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and has **no
dependency on the Test Suite workflow**. The image builds and pushes to GHCR
purely as a function of the push, never of the test outcome.

teenyverse tracks `:dev`, and the household's daily use is the canary soak. So
the canary can be running a build whose tests failed, or never ran.

Measured 2026-08-12 on the last 60 main-push Test Suite runs:

    success    29
    cancelled  26   (43%)
    failure     4

and across the last 20 main commits, 7 carry no `Test Suite Summary` check-run
at all. A cancelled run can produce zero jobs and therefore zero check-runs:
main run 31646256804 for commit 38f6ea2e1 left that commit carrying only
`merge`, `build-amd64`, `build-arm`, `ensure-mirror` — all green — and no test
verdict of any kind. `build-amd64` and `build-arm` succeeding is exactly the
point: the image shipped.

The 43% cancellation rate is mostly `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` doing its
job on rapid pushes, which is deliberate and correct. The defect is not the
cancellation; it is that the image build does not care about it.

Two related fixes have landed or are in flight and deliberately do NOT cover
this:

  - `scripts/preflight-release-tag.sh` now requires a positive
    `Test Suite Summary` verdict before an irreversible tag. That protects
    *public releases* only.
  - #1576 drops the CI-skip marker from generated translation commits, so those
    stop landing on main unverified.

Neither gates `:dev`. A user on the dev channel — which is the delivery channel
per the release policy — still receives builds from unverified commits.

Not fixed here because gating the dev image on Test Suite success changes the
delivery channel's timing and failure behaviour (a cancelled run would mean no
dev image for that commit), and that is an operator-visible tradeoff about the
household instance rather than a straightforward correctness fix. Options worth
weighing: make the dev build a `workflow_run` consumer of a successful Test
Suite; or keep building but have teenyverse's pull step refuse a digest whose
commit lacks a green verdict.
title: The :dev image publishes from commits whose Test Suite never passed
